deviations: D1: FastEndpoints serializer required explicit JsonStringEnumConverter. System.Text.Json does not deserialize string enum values by default. Adding `c.Serializer.Options.Converters.Add(new JsonStringEnumConverter())` to `UseFastEndpoints(...)` in Program.cs fixed deserialization of `PaymentType` ('Cash') from JSON string → enum. This also makes all response enum fields serialize as strings (not integers) which is the correct JSON API convention. EF Core's enum-as-string convention is DB-side only and orthogonal. Prior session's debug test confirmed: POST orders/{id}/complete with paymentType='Cash' returned 500 (System.Text.Json.JsonException propagated through DontCatchExceptions → global handler).

D2: ActorResolver shared static class in Features/Orders/Shared/ resolves the caller's JWT claims (sub, role) into an Actor. For Driver callers it queries Drivers table by UserId to get the Driver row ID. Returns null if sub is missing/unparseable, role is unrecognized, or driver row not found — callers return 404 (no-leak). This is a shared helper across all 8 transition endpoints to avoid code duplication without introducing a service class.

D3: AssignOrderEndpoint resolves the Driver row from the DB (tenant-scoped via global query filter) before passing driver.Id and driver.CurrentVehicleId to AssignPayload. Cross-tenant driver IDs return 404 because the query filter excludes rows from other fleets.

D4: CancelOrderEndpoint uses no Policies() call. Any authenticated role may attempt cancel; the state machine's NotEntitled result handles unauthorized callers with a no-leak 404. This matches the spec's cancel-policy: Dispatcher (New/Assigned/Accepted/Arrived), Customer (New/Assigned/Accepted), Driver (Arrived, ≥5 min after ArrivedAt). All other callers get 404.

D5 (CORRECTED by round-2 fix): The original D5 claim that 'FluentValidation validators registered via FastEndpoints do fire on HTTP requests' was incorrect. Root cause: FastEndpoints' DontCatchExceptions() disables the framework's own catch that converts ValidationFailureException into a 400. When a Validator<T> (registered with FastEndpoints) fails, it throws ValidationFailureException before HandleAsync; DontCatchExceptions() lets it propagate to the global exception handler as a 500. The inline guards were not redundant — they were the only working path. Round-2 fix: added ValidationFailureExceptionHandler (IExceptionHandler, Common/ValidationFailureExceptionHandler.cs) registered before AddProblemDetails() in Program.cs. It intercepts ValidationFailureException and writes a 400 ProblemDetails response; all other exceptions fall through to the 500 handler. After this fix, the three Validator<T>-based validators (Decline, Cancel, Complete) fire correctly over HTTP and the inline guards were deleted. Three integration tests (Decline_EmptyReason_Returns400, Cancel_EmptyReason_Returns400, Complete_MissingPaymentType_Returns400) now prove the validator path — HandleAsync no longer contains any 400-emitting code for these inputs, so the only way the tests can pass is via the validator.
D6: Scratch debug test file OrderTransitionDebugTest.cs (left by the turn-capped prior session) was deleted. It contained two failing tests that were diagnostic scaffolding, not production tests.
D7: Test name 'Complete_FixedPriceMismatchWithoutReason_Returns409' was used instead of the spec's 'Complete_FixedPriceOverrideNoReason_Returns409'. Same behavior tested. No functional impact.

D8 (round-2 F2): isAssignedDriver was hardcoded as false in Assign, Reassign, Decline, Complete endpoints and computed without actor.DriverId.HasValue guard in Accept, Arrive, Start. All 8 transition endpoints now uniformly compute: isAssignedDriver = actor.DriverId.HasValue && order.DriverId == actor.DriverId.
D9 (round-2 F3): OrderTransitionValidatorTests class was not sealed. Sealed in round-2.
